name: Assessment centre (interpersonal exercises: role-play, group discussion, presentation)
native_mode: observer rating of live or recorded simulations by trained assessors

A1.why: G-study (inter-assessor): .80 single post-exercise rating, .97 overall; but across exercises only .26 (single rating), .55 (dimension over 3 exercises), .65 (overall over 3) - adequate across assessors, inadequate across situations; narrative figure .70 in salgado2008.

A2.why: Contested: person x dimension variance .13-1.11% vs exercise 24.7-53.7% (jackson2016); exercise 41% vs broad dimensions 13% (hoffman2011); meta-analytic CFA prefers 3 broad factors with relational skills least supported (meriac2014, abstract); kuncel_sackett2014 argues the opposite (secondary).

A3.why: Re-estimated meta-analytic operational validity .29 vs job performance (sackett2022); dimensions .25-.39 (arthur2003, abstract); +.10 R2 over GMA + Big Five (meriac2008, N=52,779).

A4.why: Evidence from independent academics; overall-score criterion validity held after Sackett's re-estimation.

A5.why: Meta-analytic N=52,779 (meriac2008), operational AC N=698 (jackson2016), 4 field samples incl. 1,075 bank candidates (hoffman2011); 2008-2022.

A6.why: Exercise effects dominate; role-player disposition changes candidate behaviour (oliver2014); the most conversational dimensions add least (communication dR2 .003 n.s., consideration .005; meriac2008).

B1.why: Independent surveys: UK AC 17.3%, group exercise 14.9% (zibarras2010); Germany 35% (diekmann_konig); Spanish SMEs 8% (alonso2015); 52% in a large-firm Spanish convenience sample (cop_madrid, professional body).

B2.why: International Taskforce Guidelines define the method (multiple simulations, multiple trained assessors, FOR training).

B3.why: Face validity drives perceived fairness (hausknecht2004, secondary); adverse-impact figures for ACs not found.

B4.why: No Spanish instrument; built locally and practised in Spain (alonso2015, cop_madrid); Spanish-journal rater-accuracy work (wirz2013).

C1.why: Native mode is trained-observer rating of interaction; Guidelines allow rating post hoc from audio/video recordings (p. 1251).

C2.why: One study: ML on manual transcripts of 18 three-minute role-plays converged with assessors about as well as one human; ASR abandoned for room noise.

C4.why: Method is free and the Guidelines open; indicators must come from one's own job analysis (vendor dimension libraries are proprietary).

C5.why: Influencing others, consideration of others, communication: leadership and negotiation-like role-plays.

verdict.label: use
verdict.reason: Use as the measurement model (several situations, several trained raters, behaviour classified to job-derived dimensions); a machine may assist assessors but a fully automated scorer is not an AC under rupp2015.

disagreements: arthur2003 abstract says 6 dimensions; meriac2008 and hoffman2011 describe 7.
Dimension variance negligible (jackson2016) vs can dominate with two exercises (kuncel_sackett2014, secondary).
open_questions: How many recorded conversations per person reach .80 across situations in this product's setting (jackson2016 gives .65 for 3 exercises)?
Does transcript-only scoring keep validity when ASR and diarisation errors are present (hickman2023 used manual transcripts)?

name: Multiple speeded assessments (many 3-minute role-plays)
native_mode: observer rating of many short recorded role-plays

A1.why: Single human assessor G(q,1) averaged .38 per 3-minute role-play; single role-plays 'not ensured' reliable.

A2.why: not found (Breil 2022 on distinct social skills not obtained).

A3.why: Aggregate of 18 role-plays predicted instructor ratings 7 months later: .54 (abstract) / human OAR r=.57; MBA students, not a job criterion.

A4.why: Single independent research group and dataset.

A6.why: Individual role-plays unreliable; validity exists only in aggregate.

B4.why: No Spanish version; method described in open paper.

C2.why: One study of ML scoring of the transcripts against assessors.

C5.why: Interpersonal role-plays; specific scope constructs not recorded.

verdict.label: use-as-reference
verdict.reason: The design template for this product: many short heterogeneous scored conversations aggregated, rather than one long one.

open_questions: Which constructs were rated (Herde & Lievens 2023 full text not obtained)?
Does the format transfer from scripted role-plays to natural meetings?

name: Structured (behavioural / competency) interview
native_mode: interview: trained interviewers rate answers against anchored scales
constructs: job-related competencies elicited by past-behaviour or situational questions

A1.why: Reliability .83 reported in an independent narrative of meta-analyses (type not separated).

A2.why: not found: construct-validity meta-analysis exists (salgadomoscoso2002) but no figure was opened.

A3.why: Re-estimated meta-analytic operational validity .42, top of all predictors (sackett2022); .63 for structured behavioural interview in salgado2008 (older corrections).

A4.why: Independent; remained the top predictor after critical re-estimation.

A6.why: What is called 'structured' varies in practice; only 24.6% of HR respondents rejected an anti-structure myth (fisher2019); B-W d = .23.

B1.why: UK structured 69.4% (zibarras2010); Spain competency interview 52% of SMEs (alonso2015) and 80% (cop_madrid).

B2.why: Recommended in the Spanish professional channel (salgado_moscoso2008 abstract); no formal body standard collected.

B3.why: Seen as legally defensible (zibarras2010); small subgroup difference d=.23 (sackett2022); candidate reactions not collected first-hand.

B4.why: Practised in Spain; no standard Spanish instrument.

C1.why: Interview answers scored by assessors (answers about other situations, not live interaction).

C2.why: Indirect and partly negative: LLM ratings from interview transcripts gave R2 < 0 for job-related competences/interview performance (zhang2024, context to check); crowd-rated mock interviews (naim2015).

C4.why: Method free; questions and anchors self-built.

C5.why: Any competency incl. leadership; not specific.

verdict.label: use-as-reference
verdict.reason: Best-validated way of scoring spoken answers; use its anchoring and structure as the human criterion and design pattern, not as something the product replaces.

disagreements: Validity .42 (sackett2022) vs .51 (Schmidt & Hunter, via sackett2022) vs .63 (salgado2008) vs .70 (huffcutt2014, secondary, overcorrected).
open_questions: Can transcript scoring reach trained-interviewer agreement for competencies (zhang2024 says no for its setting)?

name: Unstructured interview
native_mode: free conversation judged by the interviewer

A2.why: not found

A3.why: Meta-analytic re-estimate .19 (sackett2022); .14 in salgado2008.

A4.why: Independent evidence; validity estimate halved under re-estimation (.38 -> .19).

A6.why: Practitioners over-trust it relative to evidence (highhouse2008; zibarras2010 authors).

B2.why: Negative: the professional-channel review recommends structured interviews instead.

B3.why: HR executives rate it above tests (Terpstra via highhouse2008); defensibility evidence not found.

verdict.label: avoid
verdict.reason: Lowest-validity interview format; do not model the product on free conversation judged globally.

name: Situational judgement test (paper or video)
native_mode: test: candidate chooses or rates responses to described situations

A2.why: Partial: knowledge instructions relate more to ability, behavioural-tendency to personality; correlate row labels partly lost in extraction.

A3.why: Meta-analysis rho .26 (k=118, N=24,756; mcdaniel2007), same .26 after re-estimation (sackett2022).

A6.why: Mostly concurrent samples; estimates rest on few studies (sackett2022 note).

B1.why: UK Civil Service uses judgement tests (owner = adopter); no independent usage figure.

C5.why: Leadership and teamwork SJTs show relatively high validity (abstract).

verdict.label: use-as-reference
verdict.reason: Useful for writing standardised scenarios that elicit the behaviour to be observed; its scoring (choosing options) is not conversation scoring.

open_questions: Christian 2010 coefficients for leadership/teamwork SJTs (abstract only).

name: Work sample / job simulation
native_mode: simulation scored by assessors

A2.why: not found

A3.why: Re-estimated meta-analytic validity .33.

A6.why: not found

B1.why: UK 19.3% (zibarras2010); Germany 37% (diekmann_konig); vendor panel 16% use, 67-68% rate effective (testgorilla2025).

B3.why: Face validity predicts perceived fairness (hausknecht2004, secondary); candidate data otherwise vendor.

B4.why: Role-play/simulations used by 20% of Spanish SMEs.

C1.why: Simulation scored by assessors on task output.

verdict.label: cite-only
verdict.reason: Supports the principle 'sample behaviour, do not ask about it', but it measures task skill, not soft skills.

name: Leaderless group discussion and leader emergence (incl. speaking time)
native_mode: observer or peer rating of who leads in an unstructured group

A1.why: not found (Bass 1954 / Bass et al. 1953 not retrieved).

A2.why: Nomological only, secondary: emergence relates to extraversion and authoritarianism (45 studies) and speaking time; Big Five R=.48 with leadership.

A3.why: not found: emergence is perception, not effectiveness; no work criterion collected.

A5.why: Student groups (256 students, secondary); meta-analyses of older work.

A6.why: Rewards talkativeness; men received about one extra vote (secondary).

B2.why: Covered as an exercise type within AC Guidelines only.

B4.why: Role-play/simulation practice in Spain (20% of SMEs); group-dynamics protocols only in grey literature.

C1.why: Native mode: observer/peer rating of live group interaction.

C2.why: Replicated automatic identification of the peer-perceived emergent leader from speaking activity (up to 80%) and speaking time effect.

verdict.label: avoid
verdict.reason: Maximum fit on paper but no work-criterion validity and a documented talkativeness/gender bias; never present emergence or speaking time as leadership skill.

open_questions: Reliability of LGD ratings (Bass et al. 1953).
Does emergence in recorded meetings relate to rated leadership effectiveness?

name: Teamwork KSA test (Stevens & Campion)
native_mode: test (situational multiple choice, 35 items)

A2.why: Contested: large correlation with aptitude tests (GMA component).

A3.why: Concurrent validity with supervisor/peer ratings in two small plant samples (n=70, 72); coefficients not seen.

A6.why: Overlap with cognitive ability.

verdict.label: cite-only
verdict.reason: Useful as a list of teamwork KSA areas; not an observational instrument.

native_mode: handwriting analysis

verdict.reason: No validity evidence; included only because 47.0% of US/Canadian HR respondents did not reject its predictive claim.

name: Big Five / FFM self-report inventories (NEO PI-R/3, BFI-2, IPIP, HEXACO)
native_mode: self-report

A1.why: Independent reviews: NEO PI-R internal consistency 4.5/5 (cop2011); conscientiousness measures reliability .80 (salgado2008). Test-retest not collected.

A2.why: Construct validity rated 3/5 for NEO PI-R by COP reviewers; structural/convergent figures not collected.

A3.why: Re-estimated meta-analytic validity: conscientiousness .19 overall (.25 contextualised), emotional stability .09, extraversion .10, agreeableness .10, openness .05 (sackett2022); conscientiousness grand mean .20 (wilmot2019).

A4.why: Independent, but the critical panel concludes self-report validity is very low for selection (morgeson2007) and estimates fell under re-estimation.

A5.why: Second-order meta-analyses: n > 1.1 million (wilmot2019), N=89,639 workers (wilmot2021).

A6.why: Faking unavoidable (morgeson2007); no DIF analysis in reviewed Spanish tests (cop2011); weaker in complex jobs (wilmot2019; salgado2017fc abstract).

B1.why: Personality questionnaires: UK 25.6% (zibarras2010), Spanish SMEs 40% (alonso2015), Germany 15% (diekmann_konig); NEO-PI only 1.9% of Spanish psychologists (muniz2020).

B2.why: SIOP supports job-linked Big Five-based assessment (statement, no data); COP review of NEO PI-R favourable with predictive validity '-'.

B3.why: Low subgroup difference (conscientiousness d=-.07); candidate reactions not collected.

B4.why: NEO PI-R Spanish adaptation rated 5/5 (cop2011); IPIP public domain (secondary).

C2.why: Negative: AVI models trained on self-reports reach convergent validity .12 (hickman2022); strangers judging from text agree only .11-.28 (connelly2010).

verdict.label: use-as-reference
verdict.reason: If personality is in scope, measure it with a short open questionnaire (e.g. IPIP) as a separate input; never infer self-report personality from transcripts.

disagreements: Conscientiousness operational validity .19-.25 (sackett2022) vs .30 (salgado2008, older corrections) vs .31 (Schmidt & Hunter via sackett2022).
open_questions: Spanish norms for an open inventory (IPIP/BFI-2 Spanish not searched).

native_mode: self-report, 170 items
constructs: 20 competencies in 5 areas incl. leadership, negotiation, communication, teamwork, influence
